newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's PM to visit Gaza for talks with Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's PM to visit Gaza for talks with Arafat.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali is expected to visit Gaza soon to hold talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on the impasse in the Middle East peace process, officials said on Tuesday.

Jordanian officials said Majali told visiting Palestinian negotiator Mahmoud Abbas that he was "looking forward to undertaking the visit soon to meet President Arafat and Palestinian officials to boost mutual ties".

Abbas briefed Majali on latest contacts with Israel to relaunch peace talks and the developments in the volatile West Bank town of Hebron, scene of daily clashes between Israeli troops and Palestinian protesters.
"This meeting comes within the framework of continued consultations between us and our brothers in Jordan," Abbas told reporters after talks with Majali.

Abbas said there was still no progress on talks to settle unresolved issues under the interim stage of the 1993 peace accords, including the Palestinian airport and safe passage corridor between Gaza and the West Bank.
"I cannot say that any achievement has been made," Abbas said.
Talks are currently aimed at paving the way for the resumption of negotiations, frozen since Israel broke ground on a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Abbas applauded Jordan for supporting Palestinian negotiators and Amman's role in trying to get the two sides back to the negotiating table.
Majali was quoted by officials as assuring Abbas that the kingdom stood by the Palestinians and extended support at all levels in their aim to gain their rights on their national soil.
In an interview last week King Hussein blamed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the breakdown in peacemaking.
